title: What Happens If You Hold In a Fart?
sources: NIDDK (NIH), 'Symptoms & Causes of Gas in the Digestive Tract': people pass gas an average of 8 to 14 times a day; up to 25 is considered normal

Clare Collins (University of Newcastle), The Conversation / ScienceAlert, 'What happens to your body when you hold in a fart': pressure build-up causes bloating and discomfort; some gas is reabsorbed through the gut wall into the circulation and exhaled through the lungs; the rest is released later

Wilson, Batty & Dill 2004, Proc. R. Soc. B, 'Pacific and Atlantic herring produce burst pulse sounds': herring release gas bubbles from the anal duct with fast repetitive tick sounds, more at night and in groups; authors suggest a social function (not proven)

lines.text: What happens if you hold in a fart?
Well, most people pass gas eight to fourteen times a day,
because your gut never stops making it.
Hold it in, and the pressure builds,
which is why your belly bloats and starts to hurt.
Some of that gas can slip through your gut wall into your blood,
lines.caps: Some of that *gas | can *slip through | your gut *wall | into your *blood

lines.text: travel to your lungs, and get breathed out.
The rest just waits, and escapes the moment you relax.

lines.text: And herring? Scientists think they use farts to stay together in the dark.
